note.after_visit_summary: You came in today with chest pressure that happens when you exert yourself, like walking uphill or carrying groceries, and goes away with rest. This is consistent with stable angina, meaning your heart isn't getting enough blood when it works hard, likely due to narrowed arteries. Your exam and ECG were normal, which can happen even with blockages. We are starting medications to protect your heart: aspirin 81 mg once daily, metoprolol 25 mg once daily, and increasing your atorvastatin from 40 mg to 80 mg at night. Continue your lisinopril 20 mg daily. You also have nitroglycerin 0.4 mg tablets to use under the tongue if chest pain occurs and doesn't go away with rest—repeat every 5 minutes up to three times if needed. Avoid heavy lifting and climbing that hill until we get your stress test results. Call 911 immediately if you have chest pain at rest, pain lasting more than 15 minutes, or if one nitroglycerin doesn't help—do not drive yourself. You will have a nuclear stress test, fasting lipid panel, and basic metabolic panel. We will see you back in about two weeks to review the results. Keep taking your medications as directed.
